title: Decision-path enrichment for live routing debug and audit
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: provide rich, searchable decision-path records and correlated trace spans to make region/tier/model_variant routing decisions debuggable in production without overwhelming storage or violating privacy. This ticket implements a compact decision-log schema, per-hop span instrumentation, sampling strategy, ingestion pipeline, dashboards, and an incremental rollout plan.

Scope:
- Decision-log record (structured) emitted for every routing evaluation containing anonymized identifiers, route inputs, policy reasons, numeric scores, chosen route, fallback metadata, and cost/latency estimates.
- Trace/span model: each routing evaluation opens a trace (trace_id) and emits spans for each hop (router-eval, region-probe, model-invocation, fallback-eval). Spans include start/end timestamps and hop-specific metrics.
- Lightweight per-hop metrics exported to ClickHouse/Prometheus for SLO dashboards (fallback-rate, regional-latency-p50/p95, tier-capacity-util).
- Sampling and retention: full decision-logs for 1% of requests by default, deterministic sampling for runway debugging (user opt-in), and tail-sampling for requests that trigger fallbacks or SLA violations. Aggregated metrics kept at higher resolution.
- Storage: decision logs shipped to BigQuery (or S3+Parquet depending on customer mode) with a columnar layout; metrics to ClickHouse for fast ad-hoc queries.
- Privacy: customer_id hashed with salted HMAC; raw prompt text redaction controlled by deployment config (private clusters may opt into full logs).

Non-goals:
- Long-term archival schema changes; this ticket focuses on realtime/debugging surface and short-term retention.

Implementation notes:
- Router service: add structured event emitter that writes decision-log JSON to kafka topic "routing-decision-events". New payload size capped at 4KB by default.
- Model proxies: emit span annotations (cache_hit, variant, latency_ms, tokens_in/out).
- Trace propagation: use existing trace_id from request if present; fallback to new trace id. B3/OTel headers supported.
- Sampling hooks: deterministic hash(request_id) for consistent 1% sampling; tail-sampling triggered by fallback_reason != null or latency_ms > threshold.
- Telemetry schema versioning: route_policy_version included so older logs remain interpretable.
- Cost estimate: ~4k QPS => ~1.2M decision-log rows/day; projected storage $1200/month on column store with 14-day hot retention.

Deliverables:
- New decision-log schema and telemetry_fields checklist (see telemetry_fields_schema).
- Router and proxy instrumentation PRs and integration tests.
- ClickHouse and BigQuery ingestion jobs + sample dashboards.
- Alerting rules for anomalous fallback spikes and cross-region latencies.

Risks & mitigations:
- Noise/cost: cap payload size, use deterministic sampling, allow admin-configured retention.
- Privacy: default redact PII and hash customer_id. Private deployments can enable more verbose logs under contract.
- Backward compatibility: include schema_version and route_policy_version; maintain thin shim to accept legacy logs for 3 months.
comments: 2025-02-11 — Asha: Initial spec reviewed in engineering sync. Agreed to keep default sampling at 1% and tail-sampling for fallbacks. Action: Marco to prototype router emitter.
2025-02-13 — Marco: Proof-of-concept emitting minimal decision-log to kafka completed. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/5123

acceptance_criteria: Router emits structured decision-log JSON to kafka topic for 100% of requests in dark-launch mode
Trace and spans show per-hop timings in tracing UI and correlate to decision-log via trace_id
Dashboards display fallback-rate, regional p95 latency, and tier utilization with <1 minute freshness
Sampling respects deterministic and tail-sampling rules and reduces avg per-day rows by >=95% versus full logging
Privacy safeguards active: customer_id hashed and prompt text redacted by default
rollout_steps: Phase 0 (dark launch): enable emission to kafka in staging and route to dev BigQuery dataset (48-72 hours)
Phase 1 (internal): dark launch to prod pipeline but consumers disabled; run cost & volume analysis (7 days)
Phase 2 (observability on): enable downstream ingestion to ClickHouse/BigQuery for sampled records and enable dashboards (14 days)
Phase 3 (opt-in customers): provide opt-in higher retention for enterprise customers and private deploys (ASAP after Phase 2)
Phase 4 (SLA): add alerts and automated anomaly detection; flip default sampling if necessary
storage_cost_estimate: $1200/month projected for 14-day hot retention on column-store; incremental ClickHouse hosting $600/month
